propositions: Fresh clone fails with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed' when two bundle objects exist for one ref in S3, rendering the store unclonable.
git-remote-s3's cmd_push rejects pushes while bundles>1 and upstream's Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is interactive-only and discards non-chosen heads, losing events unique to divergent branches.

Rebar's existing sync._do_reconverge/_union_merge already losslessly reconciles divergent ref heads via iterated 2-parent merges with no merge=union driver (UUID event dirs never collide; .bridge_state/* uses merge=ours), providing the merge semantics needed for S3 healing.

S3 multi-bundle state is ordinary ref divergence hidden at bundle-storage layer; healing requires S3 object writes/deletes (put merged bundle, delete originals) plus cross-clone serialization via the helper's per-ref conditional-put lock.
Healing algorithm must write merged tip before any delete and never delete it, preserving at least one lossless bundle at every crash point (write-then-delete ordering guarantees recover-on-retry).

Detection of multi-bundle signature ('multiple bundles exists on server', 'multiple updates for ref') in push stderr triggers optional auto-heal with one-attempt cap, followed by push retry, avoiding infinite non-FF retry loops under contention.
